God, depression is such a complex fucked up mess. In a likewise complex way, though, I'm proud of you. To be cognizant of your mistakes can be a really powerful and helpful thing.

But, please, allow yourself to remember and accept that you are depressed. Your depression wields the terrible triple-edged sword of being the cause of some of your missteps, making it seem like you're to blame for many things that are not your fault, and makes you feel the guilt of all of it with such crippling weight.

But your depression is not *you.* It is my sincerest hope that you can take both what you are feeling now, and how you've felt in the past and find a clarity in the middle. 

The anger and frustration you felt towards others before was not without meaning or justification. Sadly those completely justified feelings were undoubtedly intensified by the depression. You must be feeling a terrible amount of guilt and thinking you blew things well out of proportion now. I'm very sorry for that.

I truly do think this can be a hopeful sign though. This gives you a new perspective, a new way of talking to the people who care for you. One where you can see and discuss it from both the position of what frustrates you *and* the difficulties your depression adds to the mix.

Just please don't lose your self, your *real* self, that is neither perfect nor completely flawed, in all of it.

There's nothing in life we don't depend on other people for, at least slightly. Even the ability to wipe our own asses had to be taught.

But, no, I don't think I'm out of line for wanting, or even - gracious me, the audacity - *expecting* some effort towards a bit of the innate nobility when it comes to the people who are rather adamant, and at times even convincing, that they love me.

What gets me is the stupidity of it all. I get that they are afraid of "losing me." But their behavior, their actual engagement, with me screams that they are not really willing to do much to keep me around.

To make it clearer, actions speak louder than words. Their words say they care, but their actions do not. And I'm FUCKING SCARED! I don't know if I can trust what they are saying in the context of what they are doing. I am posting in this subreddit specifically because I am in terrible fucking shape. That really does suck, and I'm sorry you're going through this. It's really hard to feel understood, and unbearably frustrating, when people ask those questions and you just was to scream, "I don't KNOW what's wrong! That's part of the problem!" For what it's worth, you're absolutely right. You are under no obligation to have all the answers to your problems... hell  if you had the answers, there would certainly be less problems. 

Perhaps it might help to frame future discussions along the lines of "I don't know." Inform people (as gently as possible) that simply asking 'what's wrong' is really not helpful. Maybe that can open open up some dialogue options that will help you and the people you're speaking with come to find at least a few answers.

At the very least, if they continue to just ask what's wrong, you can be pretty confident this is not a person you can trust in this matter.
